channel.title: Aera field notes
channel.description: What consumer wearables can and cannot measure, with the research behind each claim.

item.title: What is Zone 2 training?
item.description: Easy, conversational effort you can hold for a long time. Quiet aerobic work that slowly builds the base.

item.title: What are heart rate zones?
item.description: Five effort bands from your working range so you see session shape, not one flat average.

item.title: What is overnight breathing rate?
item.description: Breaths per minute while you sleep. A sustained drift from your own usual is the useful signal.

item.title: What moved my recovery?
item.description: Often a hard training day or a short night relative to your own usual. Co-occurrence is not proof of cause.

item.title: Why does the week matter for stress?
item.description: The same hard day lands differently after a calm week than after several rough ones. Read the week, not only the day.

item.title: What does all-day heart rate tell me?
item.description: The spread of samples across the day, hour by hour, not one averaged number that hides the peaks and quiet floors.

item.title: What is sleep architecture?
item.description: The shape of a night: light, deep, and dreaming sleep in waves, plus how unbroken they were.

item.title: What does a hard day cost me?
item.description: Usually a quieter next-morning recovery read. One pairing is not proof of cause.

item.title: How do I balance push and rest?
item.description: Match today's effort to how recovered you actually are, not to a fixed plan.

item.title: How fast should my heart settle after exercise?
item.description: A quick drop in the first minute after hard effort is a cleaner fitness signal than one day's resting rate.

item.title: What is VO2max on a watch?
item.description: An estimate of cardiorespiratory fitness from outdoor pace and heart rate, not a lab mask measurement.

item.title: How much time asleep vs time in bed?
item.description: Time asleep is actual sleep. Time in bed includes wake. Habitual duration has a sweet spot, not a finish line.

item.title: What is a bedtime window?
item.description: A useful time band to aim for tonight, not a promise of the exact minute sleep will arrive.

item.title: What does stress mean on a watch?
item.description: A heart-rhythm activation read, often from overnight samples, not a verdict on your day.

item.title: What is training strain?
item.description: Today's heart-rate load next to the base built over recent weeks. Context, not a prescription.

item.title: What does recovery actually measure?
item.description: Overnight heart and breath signals against your own usual, not a sleep score and not a health grade.

item.title: What is sleeping heart rate?
item.description: The quieter overnight floor of your pulse, different from daytime resting rate, best read against your own nights.

item.title: What is my body clock / circadian rhythm?
item.description: An inner roughly 24-hour timing system. Watches see sleep timing steadiness, not the clock itself.

item.title: What is sleep debt?
item.description: Short nights stack as a running shortfall against what you need. Feeling less tired does not mean the deficit is gone.

item.title: Does sleep regularity matter more than duration?
item.description: Consistency of bedtime and wake often tracks health risk as strongly as hours slept, and sometimes more.

item.title: What does a sleep score mean?
item.description: A single number that folds duration, continuity, and stage estimates together. Trust the week, and trust duration before stage labels.

item.title: What is HRV?
item.description: Heart rate variability is the tiny change in spacing between beats, not how fast your heart goes. Yours only means something against your own nights.

item.title: What does a readiness score mean?
item.description: A training call from recent load, sleep debt, and overnight signals, not a health grade and not the same as one night of recovery.

item.title: Why is my resting heart rate up?
item.description: One high morning is usually noise. A run of mornings above your own range is the signal worth noticing.

item.title: How much sleep do I actually need?
item.description: There is no universal eight-hour rule. Sleep need is personal, and regularity often matters as much as duration.

item.title: Are Apple Watch sleep stages accurate?
item.description: Consumer watch stage charts look precise. Against lab sleep, they are estimates. Duration is the sturdier signal.
